page: Amazon Web Services r6gd.medium is an entry-level memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the arm64 AWS Graviton2 processor using the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. The instance features 1 dedicated physical core (1 vCPU) clocked at 2.5 GHz, configured with 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It incorporates hardware-accelerated AES cryptography instructions, while omitting vector extensions such as AVX. The server provides 8.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and includes 59 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD instance storage.

Benchmark data reflects the capabilities and limitations of its single dedicated core architecture. The instance delivered a stress-ng single-core score of 1471.08, with multi-core metrics showing identical throughput due to the single-vCPU provisioning. In synthetic testing, Geekbench scores reached 910.0 for single-core execution and 919.0 for multi-core workloads. Memory subsystem benchmarks demonstrated 19.08 GB/sec on large read operations and 9.79 GB/sec on large write operations. In application-focused metrics, the configuration achieved 1.13 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving rate of 1.17 GB/sec.

The r6gd.medium provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy deployments that do not demand parallel multi-threaded compute. By pairing 8.0 GB of RAM and high-speed local NVMe storage with a single core, it avoids the expense of unneeded compute capacity. The primary tradeoff is bounded CPU capacity and low baseline network bandwidth, which restricts suitability for compute-bound or network-heavy throughput. Recommended workloads include small Redis or Memcached instances, staging environments, lightweight relational databases using local scratch space, and data ingestion microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services r6gd.medium is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an arm64 AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.5 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. Configured with 1 dedicated physical core (1 vCPU) and 8.0 GB of RAM, it maintains an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio tailored for memory-bound tasks. The instance includes 59 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage for low-latency ephemeral caching, without discrete GPU hardware. Single-core performance is solid for its class, logging 1471.08 in stress-ng and 1.13 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Compute capacity is fundamentally restricted by the single-thread allocation, making the r6gd.medium an economical choice specifically for low-concurrency in-memory caching, microservices, and lightweight database workloads.
